intuition: At each letter, choose to keep it or omit it. Count consecutive omitted letters rather than writing a separate number for each one. Write that count just before the next kept letter, or at the end. This generates every valid abbreviation from a clear sequence of choices.

Keep a pending count alongside the already emitted prefix. Omitting a character increments the count without writing anything. Keeping a character first writes any pending count, then that letter, and resets the count. A real letter is what separates numeric runs in a valid abbreviation.

At the end, flush a remaining count even if no later letter exists to trigger it. Every keep-or-omit pattern follows one recursion path, so all abbreviations appear exactly once. Passing immutable prefixes keeps sibling decisions independent, while the count summarizes a run that has not yet been emitted.

This teaching implementation passes immutable prefix strings, making sibling branches independent but keeping O(n²) prefix characters across a recursion stack. An optional mutable token path can instead append a pending count and kept letter, recurse, then pop exactly those appended tokens; the omit branch changes only the pending counter.
Joining the token path only at a leaf reduces additional storage to O(n), with the same O(n*2^n) output cost. The undo steps must restore the shared path before exploring a sibling.

steps: For word="abc", start with i=0, path="", and count=0. Omitting all three characters grows count to 3 and emits "3" at the end.
Omit a and b but keep c: the pending count 2 is flushed before c, producing "2c".
Omit a, keep b, then omit c: emit "1b" when b is kept, then flush the final count 1 to obtain "1b1".
Keeping c on that branch instead gives "1bc". Keeping a before omitting b and c gives "a2".
The remaining keep/omit branches yield "a1c", "ab1", and "abc". Together these are all eight patterns for three letters.

codeNotes.note: An omitted character extends the pending run. Delaying its numeric representation automatically merges consecutive omissions instead of writing adjacent counts.

codeNotes.code: prefix = path + (str(count) if count else '') + word[i]
codeNotes.note: Keeping a real letter closes an omitted run. Only a nonzero count is emitted, and the letter separates it from any future omitted run.
The terminal case must flush a trailing run because there may be no kept letter after it to perform that operation.

keyDecision: Flush the pending omitted count before writing a kept letter and when the word ends.

concept.question: How can an omitted run be remembered without writing one marker per letter?
intuition: Choosing whether to keep each letter produces all possibilities, but writing a separate 1 for every omitted letter would create ambiguous or noncanonical adjacent counts.
Walk along the word with a count of consecutive omitted letters. Omitting extends that run; keeping a letter first writes the pending count, then the letter. At the end, write any remaining run once.
concept.observation: An omission count represents one consecutive run, and is flushed before the next kept letter.
approach: Branch at each letter: omit it or keep it.
Accumulate consecutive omissions into one count.
Flush that count before a kept letter or at the word’s end.
concept.correctness: Every subset of kept positions determines one branch path and one abbreviation. Consecutive omitted positions are represented by their exact run length, while kept letters separate runs. This gives every valid abbreviation and prevents two branch paths from producing the same canonical pattern.

complexity.space: O(n^2) auxiliary with copied prefixes, excluding output
complexity.explanation: There are two choices at each of the word’s positions, so output is exponential. Writing each abbreviation takes up to the word length; the recursive choice path is linear in depth, with additional copying work for constructed prefixes.
